paper_metadata.title: Monte-Carlo Option Pricing in Quantum Parallel

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based Monte Carlo option-pricing-in-quantum-parallel (MCQP) algorithm for European call options under BSM dynamics, with circuit depth O(m) and circuit size approximately n + kp + (kv + ks)·d + log(m) + 1. It reports only classical simulations: 10,000-path pricing sweeps, 30-trial precision studies, and no quantum hardware execution; the main claimed benefit is a quadratic Monte Carlo error reduction via amplitude estimation, not a demonstrated practical speedup.

experiments.description: Monte-Carlo option pricing in quantum parallel (MCQP) for a single-stochastic-variable Black-Scholes-Merton European call option, with classical simulations used to study pricing accuracy versus number of simulations, time steps, and precision bits; amplitude estimation is proposed for the quantum speedup but no hardware execution is reported.

algorithm.variant: MCQP with amplitude encoding of mean payoff and optional QAMC/QAE post-processing
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not applicable; stochastic samples generated via seed-based rejection sampling and classical simulation settings fixed as above.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Stock-price, stochastic-variable, and payoff values are discretized into computational-basis bit strings in separate registers; an index register of size n=log2(N) labels N parallel paths; an ancilla qubit encodes the square root of the mean payoff amplitude.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the discounted expected payoff of a European call option, E[max(S_T-K,0)] discounted by the risk-free rate.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under geometric Brownian motion / Black-Scholes-Merton dynamics.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic BSM paths; no market dataset used.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Stochastic increments ΔW generated by seed-based rejection sampling from a normal distribution; stock and payoff values rounded/discretized to finite precision in classical emulation studies.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Classical simulations over parameter sweeps; 30 trials for the accuracy-vs-precision/time-step study; comparison against analytically solved BSM call price.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical Monte Carlo / classical emulation of discretized quantum circuit components
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Seed generation via logistic map and rejection sampling to produce approximate normal variates; discretization/rounding of values to emulate finite-precision registers.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average payoff computation and comparison to analytical BSM price; error analysis versus simulations, time steps, and precision bits.

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming amplitude estimation is applied after state preparation
speedup_claims.caveats: No hardware execution; the paper proposes MCQP as a state-preparation method enabling QAE/QAMC speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation with M applications of the operator and efficient loading
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quantum sampling error scaling but does not report a hardware benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(m) circuit depth; circuit size approximately n + kp + (kv + ks)·d + log(m) + 1
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo error scales as O(1/sqrt(N))

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A fault-tolerant implementation would need efficient state preparation for stock-price distributions, amplitude estimation, and enough logical qubits for the index, stochastic-variable, stock-price, payoff, and ancilla registers.
limiting_factors: State preparation for arbitrary distributions is identified as difficult in the paper
Classical simulations are used for validation, not quantum execution

notes: No actual quantum hardware run is reported; the paper presents a gate-based algorithm and classical simulations of its discretized behavior.

The paper states the circuit uses four quantum registers plus one ancilla, with index register size n=log(N), but does not give a single concrete total qubit count for the evaluated runs, so num_qubits is left null.
Amplitude estimation/QAMC is discussed as the speedup mechanism; the paper explicitly contrasts O(1/M) quantum sampling error with O(1/sqrt(N)) classical Monte Carlo error.
The paper proposes a gate-based MCQP algorithm and discusses quadratic error scaling via amplitude estimation, but reports no hardware benchmark or demonstrated runtime advantage.
